gaps.concept: Fibrocystic change causes bilateral, lumpy breast tenderness that worsens before menstruation and improves afterward.
gaps.why_tested: A premenopausal patient has breast pain and nodularity that fluctuate with the menstrual cycle.

gaps.concept: Fibrocystic cysts may appear as blue-domed cysts; apocrine cells have abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm.
gaps.why_tested: A gross specimen or biopsy asks for the benign lesion behind a palpable cyst.

gaps.concept: Sclerosing adenosis has increased, compressed acini within lobules and an intact myoepithelial layer; it can mimic invasive carcinoma.
gaps.why_tested: A biopsy shows distorted glands in dense stroma, but myoepithelial cells are preserved.

gaps.concept: Radial scar is a benign stellate lesion with central fibrosis and radiating entrapped ducts that can mimic carcinoma on mammography.
gaps.why_tested: A spiculated mammographic lesion proves benign on biopsy.

gaps.concept: Usual ductal hyperplasia has heterogeneous cells and irregular slitlike spaces; atypical ductal hyperplasia has uniform cells and rigid secondary spaces.
gaps.why_tested: A ductal proliferation must be classified by atypia and associated cancer risk.

gaps.concept: Intraductal papilloma contains branching fibrovascular cores lined by epithelial and myoepithelial cells.
gaps.why_tested: Histology of a subareolar lesion causing bloody discharge asks for the diagnosis.

gaps.concept: Phyllodes tumors often grow rapidly; malignant stromal cells spread hematogenously, especially to the lungs, while nodal spread is rare.
gaps.why_tested: A rapidly enlarging fibroepithelial mass is followed by distant metastasis without axillary nodal disease.

gaps.concept: Fat necrosis shows lipid-laden macrophages, multinucleated giant cells, and later fibrosis.
gaps.why_tested: A firm post-traumatic mass mimics carcinoma clinically and on imaging.

gaps.concept: Mammary duct ectasia can cause nipple retraction; dilated ducts contain debris and lipid-laden macrophages.
gaps.why_tested: An older patient has colored nipple discharge and retraction, raising concern for cancer.

gaps.concept: Periductal mastitis produces keratin plugs that obstruct ducts and may lead to recurrent subareolar fistulas.
gaps.why_tested: A smoker has repeated subareolar abscesses with a draining tract.

gaps.concept: Galactocele is a painless milk-retention cyst from duct obstruction during or after lactation; aspiration yields milky fluid.
gaps.why_tested: A recently breastfeeding patient develops a noninflamed breast mass.

gaps.concept: A first-degree family history of breast cancer further raises risk when benign biopsy shows atypical hyperplasia.
gaps.why_tested: A risk-comparison question combines family history with breast-biopsy findings.

gaps.concept: Physiologic gynecomastia occurs in newborns, puberty, and older men; it is typically symmetric and centered beneath the areola.
gaps.why_tested: A tender subareolar breast enlargement appears at a characteristic age without another illness.

gaps.concept: Spironolactone, cimetidine, antiandrogens, and anabolic steroid withdrawal are classic drug-associated causes of gynecomastia.
gaps.why_tested: A medication exposure precedes new male breast enlargement.

gaps.concept: Gynecomastia can result from primary hypogonadism, cirrhosis, hyperthyroidism, or an hCG-secreting testicular tumor.
gaps.why_tested: A male breast mass accompanies low testosterone, liver disease, thyrotoxicosis, or a testicular mass.

gaps.concept: True gynecomastia has palpable glandular tissue beneath the areola; pseudogynecomastia is adipose tissue without glandular proliferation.
gaps.why_tested: An obese man has breast enlargement, and the question asks whether glandular tissue has grown.

gaps.concept: Gynecomastia is usually concentric beneath the nipple; male breast carcinoma more often forms a hard, eccentric mass with nipple changes.
gaps.why_tested: An older man presents with unilateral breast enlargement and nipple retraction.

gaps.concept: Breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma typically presents years later as a peri-implant seroma or mass and is ALK-negative.
gaps.why_tested: Delayed swelling around a textured implant yields atypical CD30-positive cells.
